subject: Operator access & residency: bounded failover and subprocessor roster
messages:
From: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cytherahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Data sovereignty + operator access during incident windows

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move forward with the pilot, our security and legal teams asked for a clear written statement on two narrow items:

1) Operator "switchboard"/access during incident response: in the event of an operational incident that requires manual remediation, what operators (Redwood employees or subcontractors) may access customer workloads and keys? Can you provide the delegation model, whether access is recorded in audit logs, and whether any operator activity could transit outside the EU during that period?

2) Bounded failover window: we need an explicit maximum duration and conditions when processing may temporarily be routed outside the EU (e.g., overflow analytics, cache rehydration or DR). Our customers require a maximum bounded window and pre-notification when possible.

We also need an up-to-date subprocessor roster and any DPA addendum language that touches temporary cross-border processing (even if narrow and conditional). Can you send the roster, the proposed language, and an ops-runbook summary?

Our security team is at security@cytherahealth.com if you want to loop them in.

Best,
Sarah
Head of InfoSec, Cythera Health

Attachments referenced: none in this message
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@cytherahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty + operator access during incident windows

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for laying this out so clearly. Short answers up front, then concrete next steps:

- Operator access: Redwood restricts live operator access to a named on-call group; all access is time-limited, tied to a Jira incident, and recorded in immutable audit logs with keystroke-level metadata for sensitive flows. Where operator activity must touch customer data or keys, we require escalation and dual-approval; we do not perform routine maintenance that exposes raw customer content.

- Cross-border/bounded failover: For Cythera's EU production tenancy we can commit to regional processing in the EU for primary inference and storage. In emergency scenarios requiring failover (e.g., loss of region-level capacity), we will activate a conditional failover path for non-primary telemetry and ephemeral cache rehydration only. The bounded parameters we propose: planned maintenance overflow (pre-notified): up to 24 hours; emergency failover (incident-driven): up to 72 hours with written post-incident notification and an option for you to require immediate rollback sooner. Any failover that would route persistent data or long-term storage outside the EU requires DPA addendum approval.

I attached a draft DPA addendum and the current subprocessor roster for your review. Karthik and Grace are on the thread to share the ops-runbook excerpt and the telemetry/audit evidence we can provide.

Next steps:
- If the wording above fits your risk model, sign the DPA addendum we sent via DocuSign (link below).
- Karthik will follow up with the minimal ops-runbook extract and the audit retention docs.
- We can schedule a 30-minute security call tomorrow to walk your SecOps through the access model.

DocuSign (DPA addendum): https://www.docusign.com/transactions/abc123-redwood-dpa
Attachments: redwood-dpa-addendum-draft.pdf, subprocessor-roster-20261130.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Risk
Redwood Inference

Sarah —

Quick technical summary to supplement Marissa's note:

- Operator model: only SREs with designated incident roles can request devops-console elevation; every elevation creates an audited session (timestamps, commands run, files accessed). For key material stored in customer-managed KMS (recommended), we never import raw keys; for Redwood-managed KMS we use HSM-backed keys and record any operator unseal activity.

- Audit artifacts we will provide on request: time-series of operator session tokens, session duration, IP hops, and per-request audit IDs that map to token-level logs. These artifacts are retained for 1 year by default (we can extend retention in the DPA addendum).

- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists our infra partners (cloud region providers), monitoring vendors, and a small set of ops contractors in APAC for 24/7 on-call support. Importantly, APAC contractors only have access to non-sensitive monitoring telemetry and cannot access PII or model context.

- Failover mechanics: the path we use for ephemeral overflow is explicitly limited to tokenized telemetry and cache rehydration. Persistent storage write-backs to alternative regions are disabled by default; any change requires an explicit ops playbook activation with customer approval in the DPA addendum.

I've dropped a short ops-runbook excerpt in the shared Drive link below (read-only). If you need a signed attestation that we won't initiate persistent cross-border reprocessing without written approval, we can add that clause to the addendum.

Shared runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-subprocessors

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Reliability
Redwood Inference
